speaker: (the ostler)
text: A bay, if you will see him. Sound. A little sour in the morning, and sourer if you ask him to stand still and be admired.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Sour I can ride. Show me the mouth.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: The teeth, sir. I show them. I do not swear they are a scholar's teeth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am looking at them as if I knew. That is the whole of my horse-craft. He is a bay, and he is sound enough to bespeak.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: You nod at the near tooth very gravely, master. It is yellow.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It says he will argue. I am not paying for a sweeter argument.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: Twelvepence the day, and his own fodder. From Wednesday week. Nothing in hand today, if that is the bargain you want written.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Nothing in hand. Wednesday the twenty-sixth, which is Wednesday week. Twelvepence the day, and the fodder is my charge.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: Then I write the day, and not the money. The twenty-sixth. A bay. Twelvepence. Fodder apart. He will be in the stall at first light if you are at the gate.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will be at the gate on the twenty-sixth. I am not taking him this afternoon.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: And the stick under your arm, master? He shies at a sword.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is lath, and it has killed four Richmonds. He may shy at it with my blessing.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: Sour at five in the morning. He will tell you so himself. I have warned you. That is what an ostler owes.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Warned is enough. I will not ask him to be sweet about it.

speaker: (the ostler)
text: God keep you off his forehand till the twenty-sixth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: And you. The twenty-sixth. I will not come for him sooner.
